The epitope of F8.12.19 Fab on the P. falciparum AMA1 protein was determined from the crystal structure of the complex. Only the 34-residue segment (Ile479 to Arg512) of the complete PfAMA1 ectoplasmic region could be identified in the electron density. Superposition of the complete structure of the PvAMA1 ectoplasmic region [PDB:1W8K] onto the region seeing in the electron density shows that the intact antigen cannot be accommodated in the crystal lattice of the structure, suggesting that parts of the antigen were removed by proteolysis prior to crystal formation.; Unmapped quantitative response: 3D structure 2.9 angstroms

As it is called in the paper, this structure of 1F9 Fab and AMA1 (domains I+II) is in crystal form 2. The same complex in crystal form 1 is [PDB:2Q8A]. In crystal form 2, the domain II loop is disordered and AMA1 residues 355-387 were not observed in the electron density. Similarly, the domain I loop, If, was disordered (AMA1 residues 264-272). There was one gap in the heavy chain constant domain between residues H128 and H132. Mutational data highlighted the importance of of polymorphic residues 197, 200, 201, 204, and 225, and these data were consistent with the crystal structure in that these residues all present large antibody-interacting areas.; Unmapped quantitative response: 3D structure 2.3 angstroms

As it is called in the paper, this structure of 1F9 Fab and AMA1 (domains I+II) is in crystal form 1. The same complex in crystal form 2 is [PDB:2Q8B]. In crystal form 1, there were two gaps in the AMA1 structure. Both of these gaps were in the domain II loop: A: 351- 358 and 377-389. In addition, there were two electron density gaps in the heavy chain constant domain: H: 128-131 and 155-159.; Unmapped quantitative response: 3D structure 2.4 angstroms

The region recognized by epitope-reactive mAb 1F9 was determined by western blotting of constructs of chimeric proteins of AMA1 domains from Plasmodium falciparum 3D7 on a scaffold of non-reactive P. berghei ANKA AMA1. The results showed that mAb 1F9 recognized constructs containing domain 1. The epitope-specific mAb 1F9 recognized AMA1 from Plasmodium falciparum strain 3D7, but did not react with AMA1 from strains FVO, HB3, W2mef, 102-1, 7G8 and M24 on dot bots.

The epitope-specific1F9 Fab was analyzed for binding to mutated AMA1 domain I expressed on phage. Mutations were introduced at residues H200, F201, and D204 within loop Id, and residues I225 and N228 within loop Ie; all are sites of frequently occurring polymorphisms. Point mutations E197V, H200L, F201V, D204N, and I225L disrupted 1F9 binding. Point mutations N228K or D228K were partially disruptive. Point mutations at positions 196, 230, 243, and 244 had no effect on 1F9 binding.

The epitope of R31C2 Fab on P. knowlesi AMA1 was determined from the crystal structure of the complex, solved by molecular replacement. There is one complex for PkAMA1-Fab R31C2 in the asymmetric unit. The recombinant PkAMA1 construct comprises residues Pro43 to Pro387 from the PkAMA1 sequence of the P. knowlesi H strain (Domains 1 and 2; residue numbering from the first residue of the signal sequence, GeneBank accession no. XM_002259303) and an additional 23 C-terminal residues that include the c-myc tag and a hexa-His tag. The synthetic gene was adapted to P. pastoris codon usage and four potential N-glycosylation sites were mutated as follows: Asn107Lys, Ser178Asn, Asn189Glu and Ser240Arg.; Unmapped quantitative response: 3D structure 3.1 angstroms
